message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need | How it works | |---------|---------------|--------------| | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue). Each color has numbers 0‑9 (two of each 1‑9, one 0) and two of each action card: Skip, Reverse, Draw Two. Plus 4 Wild cards and 4 Wild Draw Four cards. | Shuffle the deck and deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down to form the draw pile. Turn the top card face‑up to start the discard pile. | | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or a pre‑agreed total). Points are tallied after each round. | | **Gameplay** | 1. Play proceeds clockwise (unless a Reverse changes direction). 2. On your turn, you may play **one** card that matches either the **color**, the **number**, or the **action** of the top discard. 3. If you have no playable card, you must draw one from the draw pile. If that card can be played, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Action Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. (Can only be played if you have no other playable card; otherwise, the opponent can challenge.) | | **Calling “UNO”** | When you play your **second‑to‑last** card, you must shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards all their cards. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of the cards left in opponents’ hands: numbers = face value, action cards = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. | | **Scoring** | Add the round score to the winner’s total. Play continues until someone reaches the target score (usually 500). | | **Variations** | • **House Rules** – e.g., “Draw Two” can be stacked, “Wild Draw Four” can be challenged, etc.
• **Speed Uno** – no “UNO” call, play as fast as possible.
• **Uno Attack** – uses a special card‑throwing machine. | **Quick Tips** 1. **Keep an eye on colors** – try to keep a variety so you’re not stuck with one color. 2. **Save action cards** – holding a Reverse or Draw Two can swing the game. 3. **Watch opponents’ “UNO” calls** – they’re a clue to what cards you might need to block. That’s the core of Uno! Enjoy the colorful chaos.
